task.title: Visit 6 Anglophone bookshops in Paris in one day
task.shortdesc: Follow this 3-hour walking itinerary from Concorde to the Latin Quarter, visiting six indie English bookshops. The tour ends at the Jardin du Luxembourg, where you can sit back and enjoy reading all the books you've found.

step.cmd: Start at Place de la Concorde (Métro Concorde, lines 1, 8 and 12).
From the Obélisque, walk east along Rue de Rivoli.
Visit Smith and Son at 248 Rue de Rivoli.
step.info: This Anglophone bookshop is the largest one in Paris. We recommend you focus on the newest books and magazines, and visit the tearoom upstairs.

step.cmd: Continue east to Librairie Galignani at 224 Rue de Rivoli.
step.info: Galignani was the first English bookshop on the continent. With its wooden interior and glass roof, it specialises in art books.

step.cmd: Head down to the quayside, passing the Louvre Museum on the way.
Cross the Pont Notre-Dame and visit the flower market.
Walk to Notre-Dame de Paris and stop for a photo or to cool down.
Cross the Petit Pont-Cardinal Lustiger, just south of the cathedral.
Stop at Shakespeare and Company at 37 Rue de la Bûcherie.
step.info: The most famous bookshop in Paris. Don't miss the reading room upstairs!

step.cmd: Cross the street to The Abbey Bookshop at 29 Rue de la Parcheminerie.
step.info: In this Canadian-owned bookshop, jazz music is always playing. Lose yourself in this little shop brimming with books, which feels like a real maze.

step.cmd: Walk 8 minutes west to San Francisco Book Company at 17 Rue Monsieur le Prince.
step.info: The cosiest second-hand bookshop with a californian vibe. Stock up on American literature here!

step.cmd: Continue south to The Red Wheelbarrow Bookstore at 9 Rue de Médicis.
step.info: This charming indie shop is the last stop on the itinerary. Behind this iconic and timeless blue storefront lies a carefully curated selection of books.

step.cmd: As you leave the bookshop, pop into the Jardin du Luxembourg to dive into your newly found worlds.

taskbody.result: And that's how your best day in Paris comes to an end! Hope you enjoyed it :)
